newsitem.title: SPAIN: Ecuador says seeking IMF standby agreement.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador says seeking IMF standby agreement.

text.p: Ecuador's interim government is seeking a standby agreement with the International Monetary Fund, Ecuadorean Central Bank general manager Fidel Jaramillo said on Tuesday.
"We are looking for a standby agreement with the IMF," said Jaramillo, who added that an IMF mission was due to travel to Quito on April 9 to continue talks.
Jaramillo was due to meet the IMF's director for the Western Hemisphere, Claudio Loser, on the fringes of the Inter-American Development Bank's annual assembly.
The central banker declined to say when Ecuador might secure an agreement or whether the deal would include an IMF loan.

Earlier on Tuesday, Loser told Reuters that the IMF was still studying the results of a recent mission to Ecuador, where an interim administration took power last month and scrapped ousted president Abdala Bucaram's economic plan.

Asked about the incoming government's economic measures, which included an emergency fiscal tightening, Loser replied: "we have to analyse them in greater detail. I think they have the best intentions of fixing a complex situation, and we hope to work with them in the coming months to see whether we can support them concretely".
